Under this policy, a bank holding company is expected to stand ready to provide<span style="display:inline-block;height:6.93pt"></span></span><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;left:562.38pt;position:var(--position);white-space:pre;width:2.5pt"> <span style="display:inline-block;height:6.93pt"></span></span></div><div style="line-height:10pt;position:var(--position);text-align:justify;text-align-last:var(--justify);top:198.75pt;width:612pt"><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;left:49.5pt;position:var(--position);white-space:pre;width:513pt">adequate capital funds to its subsidiary bank during periods of financial adversity and to maintain financial flexibility and<span style="display:inline-block;height:6.93pt"></span></span><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;left:562.5pt;position:var(--position);white-space:pre;width:2.5pt"> <span style="display:inline-block;height:6.93pt"></span></span></div><div style="line-height:10pt;position:var(--position);text-align:justify;text-align-last:var(--justify);top:210.75pt;width:612pt"><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;left:49.5pt;position:var(--position);white-space:pre;width:512.87pt">capital raising capacity to assist its subsidiary bank. The Dodd-Frank Act codified the source of strength doctrine by adopting a<span style="display:inline-block;height:6.93pt"></span></span><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', The Bank&#8217;s ability to pay dividends is subject to various regulatory restrictions.<span style="display:inline-block;height:6.93pt"></span></span><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;left:413.85pt;position:var(--position);white-space:pre;width:5pt">&#160; It is the policy of the<span style="display:inline-block;height:6.93pt"></span></span><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;left:562.48pt;position:var(--position);white-space:pre;width:2.5pt"> <span style="display:inline-block;height:6.93pt"></span></span></div><div style="line-height:10pt;position:var(--position);text-align:justify;text-align-last:var(--justify);top:330.75pt;width:612pt"><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;left:49.5pt;position:var(--position);white-space:pre;width:512.91pt">Federal Reserve that bank holding companies should pay cash dividends only out of income available over the past year and<span style="display:inline-block;height:6.93pt"></span></span><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;left:562.41pt;position:var(--position);white-space:pre;width:2.5pt"> <span style="display:inline-block;height:6.93pt"></span></span></div><div style="line-height:10pt;position:var(--position);text-align:justify;text-align-last:var(--justify);top:342.75pt;width:612pt"><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;left:49.5pt;position:var(--position);white-space:pre;width:512.86pt">only if prospective earnings retention is consistent with the company&#8217;s expected future needs and financial condition. style="line-height:10pt;position:var(--position);text-align:justify;text-align-last:var(--justify);top:648.35pt;width:612pt"><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:bold;left:49.5pt;position:var(--position);white-space:pre;width:162.41pt">Anti-Money Laundering Act of 2020.<span style="display:inline-block;height:6.93pt"></span></span><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;left:211.91pt;position:var(--position);white-space:pre;width:350.46pt">&#160; The Anti-Money Laundering Act of 2020 (&#8220;AML Act&#8221;) was enacted as part of the<span style="display:inline-block;height:6.93pt"></span></span><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Department to issue National Anti-Money Laundering and<span style="display:inline-block;height:6.93pt"></span></span><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', occurred in June 2021.&#160; The AML Act also includes a<span style="display:inline-block;height:6.93pt"></span></span><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;left:49.5pt;position:var(--position);white-space:pre;width:512.92pt">requirement to conduct studies and issue regulations that may alter some of the due diligence, recordkeeping and reporting<span style="display:inline-block;height:6.93pt"></span></span><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', The AML Act also promotes increased information-<span style="display:inline-block;height:6.93pt"></span></span></div><div the BSA and includes whistleblower incentives, both of<span style="display:inline-block;height:6.93pt"></span></span><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', style="display:inline-block;height:6.93pt"></span></span></div></div></div><div style="--justify:justify;--position:absolute;background-color:#FFFFFF;border:1px solid #CCCC;content-visibility:auto;float:none;font-family:Arial, Sans Serif;font-size:0;height:792pt;margin:10px auto 10px style="display:inline-block;height:6.93pt"></span></span><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', maintain minimum<span style="display:inline-block;height:6.93pt"></span></span><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', The Federal Reserve establishes capital standards applicable to all bank holding companies, and the<span style="display:inline-block;height:6.93pt"></span></span><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;left:562.35pt;position:var(--position);white-space:pre;width:2.5pt"> <span style="display:inline-block;height:6.93pt"></span></span></div><div style="line-height:10pt;position:var(--position);text-align:justify;text-align-last:var(--justify);top:78.75pt;width:612pt"><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;left:49.5pt;position:var(--position);white-space:pre;width:512.94pt">WDFI and FDIC establish capital standards applicable to Washington state chartered, non-member banks. The capital rules<span style="display:inline-block;height:6.93pt"></span></span><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;left:562.44pt;position:var(--position);white-space:pre;width:2.5pt"> <span style="display:inline-block;height:6.93pt"></span></span></div><div style="line-height:10pt;position:var(--position);text-align:justify;text-align-last:var(--justify);top:90.75pt;width:612pt"><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;left:49.5pt;position:var(--position);white-space:pre;width:512.86pt">reflect, in part, certain standards initially adopted by the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision in December 2010 (which<span style="display:inline-block;height:6.93pt"></span></span><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;left:562.36pt;position:var(--position);white-space:pre;width:2.5pt"> <span style="display:inline-block;height:6.93pt"></span></span></div><div style="line-height:10pt;position:var(--position);text-align:justify;text-align-last:var(--justify);top:102.75pt;width:612pt"><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;left:49.5pt;position:var(--position);white-space:pre;width:452.5pt">standards are commonly referred to as &#8220;Basel III&#8221;) as well as requirements contemplated by the Dodd-Frank Act.<span style="display:inline-block;height:6.93pt"></span></span><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;left:502pt;position:var(--position);white-space:pre;width:5pt">&#160; <span style="display:inline-block;height:6.93pt"></span></span></div><div style="line-height:10pt;position:var(--position);text-align:justify;text-align-last:var(--justify);top:126.75pt;width:612pt"><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;left:72pt;position:var(--position);white-space:pre;width:490.3pt">The capital rules require a capital ratio of common equity Tier 1 capital to risk based assets. Common equity Tier 1 capital<span style="display:inline-block;height:6.93pt"></span></span><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', the Company and the Bank exercise a one-time irrevocable<span style="display:inline-block;height:6.93pt"></span></span><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Bank have done. Tier 1 capital also includes non-<span style="display:inline-block;height:6.93pt"></span></span></div><div style="line-height:10pt;position:var(--position);text-align:justify;text-align-last:var(--justify);top:174.75pt;width:612pt"><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;left:49.5pt;position:var(--position);white-space:pre;width:512.87pt">cumulative perpetual preferred stock and limited amounts of minority interests. Regulatory deductions from capital include<span style="display:inline-block;height:6.93pt"></span></span><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;left:562.37pt;position:var(--position);white-space:pre;width:2.5pt"> <span style="display:inline-block;height:6.93pt"></span></span></div><div style="line-height:10pt;position:var(--position);text-align:justify;text-align-last:var(--justify);top:186.75pt;width:612pt"><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;left:49.5pt;position:var(--position);white-space:pre;width:512.92pt">goodwill and intangible assets. The capital rules prescribe the manner in which certain capital elements are determined,<span style="display:inline-block;height:6.93pt"></span></span><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;left:562.42pt;position:var(--position);white-space:pre;width:2.5pt"> <span style="display:inline-block;height:6.93pt"></span></span></div><div style="line-height:10pt;position:var(--position);text-align:justify;text-align-last:var(--justify);top:198.75pt;width:612pt"><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;left:49.5pt;position:var(--position);white-space:pre;width:512.89pt">including but not limited to, requiring certain deductions related to mortgage servicing rights and deferred tax assets.&#160; Total<span style="display:inline-block;height:6.93pt"></span></span><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;left:562.39pt;position:var(--position);white-space:pre;width:2.5pt"> <span style="display:inline-block;height:6.93pt"></span></span></div><div style="line-height:10pt;position:var(--position);text-align:justify;text-align-last:var(--justify);top:210.75pt;width:612pt"><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;left:49.5pt;position:var(--position);white-space:pre;width:512.94pt">capital consists of Tier 1 capital&#160; and supplementary capital. Supplementary capital consists of certain capital instruments that<span style="display:inline-block;height:6.93pt"></span></span><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;left:562.44pt;position:var(--position);white-space:pre;width:2.5pt"> <span style="display:inline-block;height:6.93pt"></span></span></div><div style="line-height:10pt;position:var(--position);text-align:justify;text-align-last:var(--justify);top:222.75pt;width:612pt"><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;left:49.5pt;position:var(--position);white-space:pre;width:512.88pt">do not qualify as core capital as well as general valuation loan and lease loss allowances up to a maximum of 1.25% of risk-<span style="display:inline-block;height:6.93pt"></span></span></div><div style="line-height:10pt;position:var(--position);text-align:justify;text-align-last:var(--justify);top:234.75pt;width:612pt"><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;left:49.5pt;position:var(--position);white-space:pre;width:512.88pt">weighted assets. Supplementary capital may be used to satisfy the risk-based requirement only in an amount equal to the<span style="display:inline-block;height:6.93pt"></span></span><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;left:562.38pt;position:var(--position);white-space:pre;width:2.5pt"> <span style="display:inline-block;height:6.93pt"></span></span></div><div style="line-height:10pt;position:var(--position);text-align:justify;text-align-last:var(--justify);top:246.75pt;width:612pt"><span style="display:inline-block;height:6.93pt"></span></span><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', including certain off-balance-sheet items, are<span style="display:inline-block;height:6.93pt"></span></span><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', type of assets held by an institution. The risk categories<span style="display:inline-block;height:6.93pt"></span></span><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;left:562.44pt;position:var(--position);white-space:pre;width:2.5pt"> <span style="display:inline-block;height:6.93pt"></span></span></div><div style="line-height:10pt;position:var(--position);text-align:justify;text-align-last:var(--justify);top:294.75pt;width:612pt"><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;left:49.5pt;position:var(--position);white-space:pre;width:512.94pt">range from 0% for low-risk assets such as U.S. Treasury securities and GNMA securities to 1,250% for various types of loans<span style="display:inline-block;height:6.93pt"></span></span><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;left:562.44pt;position:var(--position);white-space:pre;width:2.5pt"> <span style="display:inline-block;height:6.93pt"></span></span></div><div style="line-height:10pt;position:var(--position);text-align:justify;text-align-last:var(--justify);top:306.75pt;width:612pt"><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;left:49.5pt;position:var(--position);white-space:pre;width:512.93pt">and other assets deemed to be of higher risk. Single-family residential loans having loan-to-value ratios not exceeding 90% and<span style="display:inline-block;height:6.93pt"></span></span><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', The rules set forth the methods of calculating certain risk-based assets, which in<span style="display:inline-block;height:6.93pt"></span></span><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;left:562.43pt;position:var(--position);white-space:pre;width:2.5pt"> <span style="display:inline-block;height:6.93pt"></span></span></div><div style="line-height:10pt;position:var(--position);text-align:justify;text-align-last:var(--justify);top:354.75pt;width:612pt"><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;left:49.5pt;position:var(--position);white-space:pre;width:512.87pt">turn affects the calculation of risk-based ratios. Higher or more sensitive risk weights are assigned to various categories of<span style="display:inline-block;height:6.93pt"></span></span><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;left:562.37pt;position:var(--position);white-space:pre;width:2.5pt"> <span style="display:inline-block;height:6.93pt"></span></span></div><div style="line-height:10pt;position:var(--position);text-align:justify;text-align-last:var(--justify);top:366.75pt;width:612pt"><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Of the states whose privacy laws provide data-level<span style="display:inline-block;height:6.93pt"></span></span><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;left:562.5pt;position:var(--position);white-space:pre;width:2.5pt"> <span style="display:inline-block;height:6.93pt"></span></span></div><div style="line-height:10pt;position:var(--position);text-align:justify;text-align-last:var(--justify);top:258.75pt;width:612pt"><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;left:49.5pt;position:var(--position);white-space:pre;width:512.83pt">exemptions, we are subject to the laws of California. In California, the Company must generally comply with its privacy laws<span style="display:inline-block;height:6.93pt"></span></span><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', privacy rights, including the right to know what personal information is collected, the right to<span style="display:inline-block;height:6.93pt"></span></span><span style="font-family:'Times New Interest rates are highly sensitive to factors beyond our control, such as general economic conditions and policies<span style="display:inline-block;height:6.93pt"></span></span><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;left:562.43pt;position:var(--position);white-space:pre;width:2.5pt"> <span style="display:inline-block;height:6.93pt"></span></span></div><div style="line-height:12pt;position:var(--position);text-align:justify;text-align-last:var(--justify);top:208.15pt;width:612pt"><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;left:49.5pt;position:var(--position);white-space:pre;width:175.1pt">set by governmental and regulatory bodies.<span style="display:inline-block;height:8.32pt"></span></span><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', serif;font-size:12pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;left:224.6pt;position:var(--position);white-space:pre;width:7pt">&#160; <span style="display:inline-block;height:8.32pt"></span></span><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;left:231.6pt;position:var(--position);white-space:pre;width:330.86pt">We principally manage interest rate risk by managing our volume and mix of our<span style="display:inline-block;height:8.32pt"></span></span><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;left:562.46pt;position:var(--position);white-space:pre;width:2.5pt"> <span style="display:inline-block;height:8.32pt"></span></span></div><div style="line-height:10pt;position:var(--position);text-align:justify;text-align-last:var(--justify);top:221.59pt;width:612pt"><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;left:49.5pt;position:var(--position);white-space:pre;width:512.94pt">earning assets and funding liabilities. If we are unable to manage this risk effectively, our business, financial condition and<span style="display:inline-block;height:6.93pt"></span></span><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;left:562.44pt;position:var(--position);white-space:pre;width:2.5pt"> <span style="display:inline-block;height:6.93pt"></span></span></div><div style="line-height:12pt;position:var(--position);text-align:justify;text-align-last:var(--justify);top:232.79pt;width:612pt"><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;left:49.5pt;position:var(--position);white-space:pre;width:201.38pt">results of operations could be materially affected.<span style="display:inline-block;height:8.32pt"></span></span><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', serif;font-size:12pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;left:250.88pt;position:var(--position);white-space:pre;width:7.2pt">&#160; <span style="display:inline-block;height:8.32pt"></span></span><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;left:258.08000000000004pt;position:var(--position);white-space:pre;width:304.33pt">Rapid changes in interest rates make it difficult for the Bank to balance its<span style="display:inline-block;height:8.32pt"></span></span><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;left:562.41pt;position:var(--position);white-space:pre;width:2.5pt"> <span style="display:inline-block;height:8.32pt"></span></span></div><div style="line-height:10pt;position:var(--position);text-align:justify;text-align-last:var(--justify);top:246.23pt;width:612pt"><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;left:49.5pt;position:var(--position);white-space:pre;width:512.88pt">loan and deposit portfolios, which may adversely affect our results of operations by, for example, reducing asset yields or<span style="display:inline-block;height:6.93pt"></span></span><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;left:562.38pt;position:var(--position);white-space:pre;width:2.5pt"> <span style="display:inline-block;height:6.93pt"></span></span></div><div style="line-height:10pt;position:var(--position);text-align:justify;text-align-last:var(--justify);top:257.43pt;width:612pt"><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;left:49.5pt;position:var(--position);white-space:pre;width:512.83pt">spreads, or having other adverse impacts on our business. Higher than expected inflation could lead to higher interest rates,<span style="display:inline-block;height:6.93pt"></span></span><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;left:562.33pt;position:var(--position);white-space:pre;width:2.5pt"> <span style="display:inline-block;height:6.93pt"></span></span></div><div style="line-height:10pt;position:var(--position);text-align:justify;text-align-last:var(--justify);top:268.63pt;width:612pt"><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;left:49.5pt;position:var(--position);white-space:pre;width:512.89pt">which could, in turn, increase the borrowing costs of our customers, making it more difficult for them to repay their loans or<span style="display:inline-block;height:6.93pt"></span></span><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;left:562.39pt;position:var(--position);white-space:pre;width:2.5pt"> <span style="display:inline-block;height:6.93pt"></span></span></div><div style="line-height:12pt;position:var(--position);text-align:justify;text-align-last:var(--justify);top:279.83pt;width:612pt"><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;left:49.5pt;position:var(--position);white-space:pre;width:412.03pt">other obligations. High interest rates could also push down asset prices and weaken economic activity. <span style="display:inline-block;height:8.32pt"></span></span><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', serif;font-size:12pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;left:461.53pt;position:var(--position);white-space:pre;width:3pt"> <span style="display:inline-block;height:8.32pt"></span></span><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;left:464.53pt;position:var(--position);white-space:pre;width:97.93pt">Conversely, falling rates<span style="display:inline-block;height:8.32pt"></span></span><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;left:562.46pt;position:var(--position);white-space:pre;width:2.5pt"> <span style="display:inline-block;height:8.32pt"></span></span></div><div style="line-height:10pt;position:var(--position);text-align:justify;text-align-last:var(--justify);top:293.27pt;width:612pt"><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;left:49.5pt;position:var(--position);white-space:pre;width:512.91pt">can initially reduce our net interest income as our floating-rate assets tend to be more immediately responsive to changes in<span style="display:inline-block;height:6.93pt"></span></span><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;left:562.41pt;position:var(--position);white-space:pre;width:2.5pt"> <span style="display:inline-block;height:6.93pt"></span></span></div><div style="line-height:10pt;position:var(--position);text-align:justify;text-align-last:var(--justify);top:304.47pt;width:612pt"><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;left:49.5pt;position:var(--position);white-space:pre;width:512.88pt">market rates than most deposit liabilities. In addition, a decline in market interest rates could increase loan prepayments, leading<span style="display:inline-block;height:6.93pt"></span></span><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;left:562.38pt;position:var(--position);white-space:pre;width:2.5pt"> <span style="display:inline-block;height:6.93pt"></span></span></div><div style="line-height:10pt;position:var(--position);text-align:justify;text-align-last:var(--justify);top:315.67pt;width:612pt"><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;left:49.5pt;position:var(--position);white-space:pre;width:233.61pt">to reinvestment in lower-yielding assets, reducing income.<span style="display:inline-block;height:6.93pt"></span></span></div><div style="line-height:10pt;position:var(--position);text-align:justify;text-align-last:var(--justify);top:340.67pt;width:612pt"><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;left:85.5pt;position:var(--position);white-space:pre;width:477pt">Our net interest income is the difference (or &#8220;spread&#8221;) between the interest earned on loans, securities and other<span style="display:inline-block;height:6.93pt"></span></span><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;left:562.5pt;position:var(--position);white-space:pre;width:2.5pt"> <span style="display:inline-block;height:6.93pt"></span></span></div><div style="line-height:10pt;position:var(--position);text-align:justify;text-align-last:var(--justify);top:351.87pt;width:612pt"><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;left:49.5pt;position:var(--position);white-space:pre;width:512.91pt">interest-earning assets and the interest paid on deposits, borrowings, and other interest-bearing liabilities. The level of net<span style="display:inline-block;height:6.93pt"></span></span><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;left:562.41pt;position:var(--position);white-space:pre;width:2.5pt"> <span style="display:inline-block;height:6.93pt"></span></span></div><div style="line-height:10pt;position:var(--position);text-align:justify;text-align-last:var(--justify);top:363.07pt;width:612pt"><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;left:49.5pt;position:var(--position);white-space:pre;width:512.97pt">interest income is a function of the average balances of interest-earning assets and interest-bearing liabilities and the spread<span style="display:inline-block;height:6.93pt"></span></span><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;left:562.47pt;position:var(--position);white-space:pre;width:2.5pt"> <span style="display:inline-block;height:6.93pt"></span></span></div><div style="line-height:10pt;position:var(--position);text-align:justify;text-align-last:var(--justify);top:374.27pt;width:612pt"><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;left:49.5pt;position:var(--position);white-space:pre;width:512.86pt">between the amounts of the yield on such assets and the cost of such liabilities. These factors are influenced by both the pricing<span style="display:inline-block;height:6.93pt"></span></span><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;left:49.5pt;position:var(--position);white-space:pre;width:512.86pt">and the mix of interest-earning assets and interest-bearing liabilities which, in turn, are impacted by such external factors as the<span style="display:inline-block;height:6.93pt"></span></span><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', the Federal Open Market Committee of the Federal<span style="display:inline-block;height:6.93pt"></span></span><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', rates. Furthermore, movements in interest rates, the pace at<span style="display:inline-block;height:6.93pt"></span></span><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', largely based on short-term interest rates, the level of which is driven by the<span style="display:inline-block;height:8.32pt"></span></span><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', However, the yields generated by long-term loans, such as single-family residential and multifamily mortgage loans,<span style="display:inline-block;height:6.93pt"></span></span><span maturities and repricing characteristics of our interest-earning assets and interest-bearing<span style="display:inline-block;height:6.93pt"></span></span><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Accordingly, fluctuations in interest rates could adversely affect our interest rate<span style="display:inline-block;height:6.93pt"></span></span><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;left:562.36pt;position:var(--position);white-space:pre;width:2.5pt"> <span style="display:inline-block;height:6.93pt"></span></span></div><div style="line-height:10pt;position:var(--position);text-align:justify;text-align-last:var(--justify);top:510.91pt;width:612pt"><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;left:49.5pt;position:var(--position);white-space:pre;width:512.94pt">spread, and, in turn, our profitability. For example, if interest rates on interest-earning assets decline more quickly than the rates<span style="display:inline-block;height:6.93pt"></span></span><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;left:562.44pt;position:var(--position);white-space:pre;width:2.5pt"> <span style="display:inline-block;height:6.93pt"></span></span></div><div style="line-height:10pt;position:var(--position);text-align:justify;text-align-last:var(--justify);top:522.11pt;width:612pt"><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;left:49.5pt;position:var(--position);white-space:pre;width:512.95pt">on interest-bearing liabilities, as we saw in our recent fiscal year, the result is a reduction in our net interest income and with it,<span style="display:inline-block;height:6.93pt"></span></span><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;left:562.45pt;position:var(--position);white-space:pre;width:2.5pt"> <span style="display:inline-block;height:6.93pt"></span></span></div><div style="line-height:12pt;position:var(--position);text-align:justify;text-align-last:var(--justify);top:533.31pt;width:612pt"><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;left:49.5pt;position:var(--position);white-space:pre;width:95.01pt">a reduction in earnings.<span style="display:inline-block;height:8.32pt"></span></span><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', serif;font-size:12pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;left:144.51pt;position:var(--position);white-space:pre;width:6.82pt">&#160; Each request for modification is individually evaluated for merit and<span style="display:inline-block;height:6.93pt"></span></span><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;left:562.36pt;position:var(--position);white-space:pre;width:2.5pt"> <span style="display:inline-block;height:6.93pt"></span></span></div><div style="line-height:10pt;position:var(--position);text-align:justify;text-align-last:var(--justify);top:141.15pt;width:612pt"><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;left:49.5pt;position:var(--position);white-space:pre;width:512.97pt">likelihood of success. the credit does not meet one of the definitions below.<span style="display:inline-block;height:6.94pt"></span></span></div><div style="font-size:12pt;line-height:10pt;position:var(--position);text-align:justify;text-align-last:var(--justify);top:672.25pt;width:612pt"><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;left:49.5pt;position:var(--position);text-decoration:none;white-space:pre;width:3.5pt">&#8226;<span style="display:inline-block;height:6.94pt"></span></span><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:normal;left:67.5pt;position:var(--position);text-decoration:none;white-space:pre;width:64.49pt">Special mention<span style="display:inline-block;height:6.94pt"></span></span><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;left:131.99pt;position:var(--position);text-decoration:none;white-space:pre;width:439.34pt"> &#8211; A special mention credit is considered to be currently protected from loss but is potentially weak. No loss<span style="display:inline-block;height:6.94pt"></span></span><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;left:571.3299999999999pt;position:var(--position);text-decoration:none;white-space:pre;width:2.5pt"> <span style="display:inline-block;height:6.94pt"></span></span></div><div style="font-size:12pt;line-height:10pt;position:var(--position);text-align:justify;text-align-last:var(--justify);top:684.25pt;width:612pt"><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;left:67.5pt;position:var(--position);text-decoration:none;white-space:pre;width:503.89pt">of principal or interest is foreseen; however, proper supervision and management attention is required to deter further<span style="display:inline-block;height:6.93pt"></span></span><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;left:571.39pt;position:var(--position);text-decoration:none;white-space:pre;width:2.5pt"> <span style="display:inline-block;height:6.93pt"></span></span></div><div style="font-size:12pt;line-height:10pt;position:var(--position);text-align:justify;text-align-last:var(--justify);top:696.25pt;width:612pt"><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;left:67.5pt;position:var(--position);text-decoration:none;white-space:pre;width:503.93pt">deterioration in the credit. Assets in this category constitute some undue and unwarranted credit risk but not to the point of<span style="display:inline-block;height:6.93pt"></span></span><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;left:571.4300000000001pt;position:var(--position);text-decoration:none;white-space:pre;width:2.5pt"> <span style="display:inline-block;height:6.93pt"></span></span></div><div style="font-size:12pt;line-height:10pt;position:var(--position);text-align:justify;text-align-last:var(--justify);top:708.25pt;width:612pt"><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;left:67.5pt;position:var(--position);text-decoration:none;white-space:pre;width:503.93pt">justifying a risk rating of substandard. The credit risk may be relatively minor yet constitutes an unwarranted risk in light of<span style="display:inline-block;height:6.93pt"></span></span><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;left:571.4300000000001pt;position:var(--position);text-decoration:none;white-space:pre;width:2.5pt"> <span style="display:inline-block;height:6.93pt"></span></span></div><div style="font-size:12pt;line-height:10pt;position:var(--position);text-align:justify;text-align-last:var(--justify);top:720.25pt;width:612pt"><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;left:67.5pt;position:var(--position);text-decoration:none;white-space:pre;width:186.98pt">the circumstances surrounding a specific asset.<span style="display:inline-block;height:6.93pt"></span></span></div></div></ix:continuation></div><div style="--justify:justify;--position:absolute;background-color:#FFFFFF;border:1px solid #CCCC;content-visibility:auto;float:none;font-family:Arial, Sans Serif;font-size:0;height:792pt;margin:10px auto 10px auto;overflow:hidden;padding:0;position:relative;width:612pt;word-wrap:break-word"><div style="position:var(--position);top:749.25pt"><div style="width:540pt"><div style="line-height:10pt;position:var(--position);top:20.17pt;width:612pt"><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;left:296.5pt;position:var(--position);white-space:pre">90<span style="display:inline-block;height:6.93pt"></span></span></div></div></div><div style="position:var(--position)"><div style="width:540pt"><div style="line-height:10pt;position:var(--position);top:25.5pt;width:612pt"><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:bold;left:224.71pt;position:var(--position);white-space:pre">WAFD, INC. AND SUBSIDIARIES<span style="display:inline-block;height:6.77pt"></span></span></div><div style="line-height:10pt;position:var(--position);top:37.5pt;width:612pt"><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:bold;left:157.55pt;position:var(--position);white-space:pre">NOTES TO THE CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS<span style="display:inline-block;height:6.77pt"></span></span></div><div style="line-height:8pt;position:var(--position);top:49.5pt;width:612pt"><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', serif;font-size:8pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:bold;left:202.67pt;position:var(--position);white-space:pre">YEARS ENDED SEPTEMBER 30, 2025, 2024, AND 2023<span style="display:inline-block;height:5.41pt"></span></span></div></div></div><ix:continuation id="f-937-7" continuedAt="f-937-8"><div><div style="font-size:12pt;line-height:10pt;position:var(--position);text-align:justify;text-align-last:var(--justify);top:81pt;width:612pt"><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;left:49.5pt;position:var(--position);text-decoration:none;white-space:pre;width:3.5pt">&#8226;<span style="display:inline-block;height:6.94pt"></span></span><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:normal;left:67.5pt;position:var(--position);text-decoration:none;white-space:pre;width:50.55pt">Substandard<span style="display:inline-block;height:6.94pt"></span></span><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;left:118.05pt;position:var(--position);text-decoration:none;white-space:pre;width:453.34pt"> &#8211; A substandard credit is an unacceptable credit. Additionally, repayment in the normal course is in jeopardy<span style="display:inline-block;height:6.94pt"></span></span><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;left:571.39pt;position:var(--position);text-decoration:none;white-space:pre;width:2.5pt"> <span style="display:inline-block;height:6.94pt"></span></span></div><div style="font-size:12pt;line-height:10pt;position:var(--position);text-align:justify;text-align-last:var(--justify);top:93pt;width:612pt"><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;left:67.5pt;position:var(--position);text-decoration:none;white-space:pre;width:503.8pt">due to the existence of one or more well defined weaknesses. In these situations, loss of principal is likely if the weakness is<span style="display:inline-block;height:6.93pt"></span></span><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;left:571.3pt;position:var(--position);text-decoration:none;white-space:pre;width:2.5pt"> <span style="display:inline-block;height:6.93pt"></span></span></div><div style="font-size:12pt;line-height:10pt;position:var(--position);text-align:justify;text-align-last:var(--justify);top:105pt;width:612pt"><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;left:67.5pt;position:var(--position);text-decoration:none;white-space:pre;width:503.96pt">not corrected. A substandard asset is inadequately protected by the current sound worth and paying capacity of the borrower<span style="display:inline-block;height:6.93pt"></span></span><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;left:571.46pt;position:var(--position);text-decoration:none;white-space:pre;width:2.5pt"> <span style="display:inline-block;height:6.93pt"></span></span></div><div style="font-size:12pt;line-height:10pt;position:var(--position);text-align:justify;text-align-last:var(--justify);top:117pt;width:612pt"><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;left:67.5pt;position:var(--position);text-decoration:none;white-space:pre;width:503.94pt">or of the collateral pledged, if any. Assets so classified will have a well-defined weakness or weaknesses that jeopardize the<span style="display:inline-block;height:6.93pt"></span></span><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;left:571.44pt;position:var(--position);text-decoration:none;white-space:pre;width:2.5pt"> <span style="display:inline-block;height:6.93pt"></span></span></div><div style="font-size:12pt;line-height:10pt;position:var(--position);text-align:justify;text-align-last:var(--justify);top:129pt;width:612pt"><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;left:67.5pt;position:var(--position);text-decoration:none;white-space:pre;width:503.91pt">collection or liquidation of the debt. Loss potential, while existing in the aggregate amount of substandard assets, does not<span style="display:inline-block;height:6.93pt"></span></span><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;left:571.4100000000001pt;position:var(--position);text-decoration:none;white-space:pre;width:2.5pt"> <span style="display:inline-block;height:6.93pt"></span></span></div><div style="font-size:12pt;line-height:10pt;position:var(--position);text-align:justify;text-align-last:var(--justify);top:141pt;width:612pt"><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;left:67.5pt;position:var(--position);text-decoration:none;white-space:pre;width:222.26pt">have to exist in individual assets risk rated substandard.<span style="display:inline-block;height:6.93pt"></span></span></div><div style="font-size:12pt;line-height:10pt;position:var(--position);text-align:justify;text-align-last:var(--justify);top:165pt;width:612pt"><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;left:49.5pt;position:var(--position);text-decoration:none;white-space:pre;width:3.5pt">&#8226;<span style="display:inline-block;height:6.94pt"></span></span><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:normal;left:67.5pt;position:var(--position);text-decoration:none;white-space:pre;width:40.56pt">Doubtful <span style="display:inline-block;height:6.94pt"></span></span><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;left:108.06pt;position:var(--position);text-decoration:none;white-space:pre;width:463.31pt">&#8211; A credit classified doubtful has all the weaknesses inherent in one classified substandard with the added<span style="display:inline-block;height:6.94pt"></span></span><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;left:571.37pt;position:var(--position);text-decoration:none;white-space:pre;width:2.5pt"> <span style="display:inline-block;height:6.94pt"></span></span></div><div style="font-size:12pt;line-height:10pt;position:var(--position);text-align:justify;text-align-last:var(--justify);top:177pt;width:612pt"><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;left:67.5pt;position:var(--position);text-decoration:none;white-space:pre;width:503.88pt">characteristic that the weakness makes collection or liquidation in full, on the basis of currently existing facts, conditions and<span style="display:inline-block;height:6.93pt"></span></span><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;left:571.38pt;position:var(--position);text-decoration:none;white-space:pre;width:2.5pt"> <span style="display:inline-block;height:6.93pt"></span></span></div><div style="font-size:12pt;line-height:10pt;position:var(--position);text-align:justify;text-align-last:var(--justify);top:189pt;width:612pt"><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;left:67.5pt;position:var(--position);text-decoration:none;white-space:pre;width:503.91pt">values, highly questionable and improbable. Fair value is based on quoted market prices, when available, for identical or similar assets or liabilities. In the absence of<span style="display:inline-block;height:6.93pt"></span></span><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;left:571.47pt;position:var(--position);text-decoration:none;white-space:pre;width:2.5pt"> <span style="display:inline-block;height:6.93pt"></span></span></div><div style="font-size:12pt;line-height:10pt;position:var(--position);text-align:justify;text-align-last:var(--justify);top:333pt;width:612pt"><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;left:40.5pt;position:var(--position);text-decoration:none;white-space:pre;width:530.87pt">quoted market prices, fair value is determined using valuation models or third-party appraisals. The following is a description of the<span style="display:inline-block;height:6.93pt"></span></span><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;left:571.37pt;position:var(--position);text-decoration:none;white-space:pre;width:2.5pt"> <span style="display:inline-block;height:6.93pt"></span></span></div><div style="font-size:12pt;line-height:10pt;position:var(--position);text-align:justify;text-align-last:var(--justify);top:345pt;width:612pt"><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;left:40.5pt;position:var(--position);text-decoration:none;white-space:pre;width:530.9pt">valuation methodologies used to measure and report the fair value of financial assets and liabilities on a recurring or nonrecurring<span style="display:inline-block;height:6.93pt"></span></span><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;left:571.4pt;position:var(--position);text-decoration:none;white-space:pre;width:2.5pt"> <span style="display:inline-block;height:6.93pt"></span></span></div><div style="font-size:12pt;line-height:10pt;position:var(--position);text-align:justify;text-align-last:var(--justify);top:357pt;width:612pt"><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;left:40.5pt;position:var(--position);text-decoration:none;white-space:pre;width:22.48pt">basis.<span style="display:inline-block;height:6.93pt"></span></span></div><div style="font-size:12pt;line-height:10pt;position:var(--position);text-align:justify;text-align-last:var(--justify);top:383pt;width:612pt"><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;left:40.5pt;position:var(--position);text-decoration:underline;white-space:pre;width:131.05pt">Measured on a Recurring Basis<span style="display:inline-block;height:6.77pt"></span></span></div><div style="font-size:12pt;line-height:10pt;position:var(--position);text-align:justify;text-align-last:var(--justify);top:400pt;width:612pt"><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:normal;left:40.5pt;position:var(--position);text-decoration:none;white-space:pre;width:258.26pt">Available-for-sale investment securities and derivative contracts<span style="display:inline-block;height:6.94pt"></span></span></div><div style="font-size:12pt;line-height:10pt;position:var(--position);text-align:justify;text-align-last:var(--justify);top:417pt;width:612pt"><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;left:40.5pt;position:var(--position);text-decoration:none;white-space:pre;width:530.87pt">Securities available for sale are recorded at fair value on a recurring basis.&#160;The fair value of debt securities are priced using model<span style="display:inline-block;height:6.93pt"></span></span><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;left:571.37pt;position:var(--position);text-decoration:none;white-space:pre;width:2.5pt"> <span style="display:inline-block;height:6.93pt"></span></span></div><div style="font-size:12pt;line-height:10pt;position:var(--position);text-align:justify;text-align-last:var(--justify);top:429pt;width:612pt"><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;left:40.5pt;position:var(--position);text-decoration:none;white-space:pre;width:530.91pt">pricing based on the securities' relationship to other benchmark quoted prices as provided by an independent third party, and under<span style="display:inline-block;height:6.93pt"></span></span><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;left:571.41pt;position:var(--position);text-decoration:none;white-space:pre;width:2.5pt"> <span Securities that are traded on active exchanges, including the Company's equity<span style="display:inline-block;height:6.93pt"></span></span><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;left:571.42pt;position:var(--position);text-decoration:none;white-space:pre;width:2.5pt"> <span style="display:inline-block;height:6.93pt"></span></span></div><div style="font-size:12pt;line-height:10pt;position:var(--position);text-align:justify;text-align-last:var(--justify);top:453pt;width:612pt"><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;left:40.5pt;position:var(--position);text-decoration:none;white-space:pre;width:442.19pt">securities, are measured using the closing price in an active market and are considered a Level 1 input method.<span style="display:inline-block;height:6.93pt"></span></span></div><div style="font-size:12pt;line-height:10pt;position:var(--position);text-align:justify;text-align-last:var(--justify);top:482pt;width:612pt"><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;left:40.5pt;position:var(--position);text-decoration:none;white-space:pre;width:530.83pt">The Company offers interest rate swaps to its variable rate borrowers who want to manage their interest rate risk. At the same time,<span style="display:inline-block;height:6.93pt"></span></span><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;left:571.33pt;position:var(--position);text-decoration:none;white-space:pre;width:2.5pt"> <span style="display:inline-block;height:6.93pt"></span></span></div><div style="font-size:12pt;line-height:10pt;position:var(--position);text-align:justify;text-align-last:var(--justify);top:494pt;width:612pt"><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;left:40.5pt;position:var(--position);text-decoration:none;white-space:pre;width:530.88pt">the Company enters into the opposite trade with a counterparty to offset its interest rate risk. The Company has also entered various<span style="display:inline-block;height:6.93pt"></span></span><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;left:571.38pt;position:var(--position);text-decoration:none;white-space:pre;width:2.5pt"> <span style="display:inline-block;height:6.93pt"></span></span></div><div style="font-size:12pt;line-height:10pt;position:var(--position);text-align:justify;text-align-last:var(--justify);top:506pt;width:612pt"><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;left:40.5pt;position:var(--position);text-decoration:none;white-space:pre;width:530.96pt">forms of fair value hedges and cash flow hedges using interest rate swaps. The fair value of these interest rate swaps are estimated<span style="display:inline-block;height:6.93pt"></span></span><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;left:571.46pt;position:var(--position);text-decoration:none;white-space:pre;width:2.5pt"> <span style="display:inline-block;height:6.93pt"></span></span></div><div style="font-size:12pt;line-height:10pt;position:var(--position);text-align:justify;text-align-last:var(--justify);top:518pt;width:612pt"><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman', serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;left:40.5pt;position:var(--position);text-decoration:none;white-space:pre;width:469.18pt">by a third party pricing service using a discounted cash flow technique. These are considered a Level 2 input method.<span style="display:inline-block;height:6.93pt"></span></span></div></ix:continuation><div
